style: Warm, playful and upbeat, like a friendly game-trailer narrator. Clear diction, natural pace, small smile in the voice.

lines.text: This is a crayon doodle. Aholo Lux3D turns it into a toy design... then a real 3D model... gives it a skeleton... and moves.
Six doodles became six fighters, each with its own weight, speed and power.
Now shove your rivals off a giant desk. Hold to charge a big slap, or dash-roll out of trouble.
But the desk fights back. Lux3D articulation split the stapler, the fan and the jack-in-the-box into parts with real joints, and the game drives those joints live.
Fall off, and you flail. That's a Lux3D swim animation, used for comedy.
The last toy standing dances, and you can download it for your 3D printer.
Every toy, skeleton, move, trap joint and print file came from the Lux3D API. The Lab page shows each step, and lets you drag the hinges yourself.
